steps.title: Reproduce the lab's published numbers
steps.note: Exact CA/ADC/ARFS reproduced from raw for 2 chambers. Lab tracker ported: trace_num==1 count equals the paper's row count in all 12 fully deposited experiments (395/395). Chamber identity firm for 415/419 rows; masks-only CA within 0.5% for 369/419. Remaining value gaps are multi-component surfaces where cl_factor needs raw actin. Group 7 has 8 undeposited chambers.

steps.title: Build per-cell death labels
steps.note: Death labels for all 502 chambers, counting only the target the tracked T cell touches; MIP_ROI_0 late 405 nm band (visits 19+, all experiments) excluded; full and 200-min windows. Any-visit rule (the lab's definition) vs paper Fig 5g: high-killing 52.1% vs 57.5%, low-killing 24.4% vs 27.0%, latrunculin 5.6% vs 4.5%. Paper gives group counts only, so no per-cell check is possible.

steps.title: Describe every chamber, and 10-20 in depth
steps.note: 5a done: 33 mask descriptors (>=1.4 um scale) for all 502 chambers, with ICC noise scores and z-pitch sensitivity. 19 reliable (ICC>=0.5); fine topography (cup asymmetry, higher Zernike modes) is mostly sweep-to-sweep noise in masks. Check (5b) pre-registered in status/step5b_preregistration.md. 10-20 in-depth chambers still to do.

steps.title: Does geometry relate to killing at all?
steps.note: Pre-registered result: association present. Within experiment, deeper cups and more T-cell protrusion at first contact go with faster killing (HR ~1.4 per SD, q<0.005), also after adjusting for contact area. But no held-out gain in predicting death across experiments (dAUC -0.02 to +0.01), and no separation of high- vs low-killing donors (n=5 vs 5). Dasatinib control: indentation and protrusion drop in 3/3 donors (pre-death mean).

steps.title: First mechanical model
steps.note: 6a done (custom two-shell model chosen over SimuCell3D). 6b first run rejected on review: solver validation was circular, and late-visit predictions were the proportional baseline times an ad hoc factor rather than per-visit solves. Rerun in progress with independent validation (flat membrane, Laplace law, tense sphere) and per-visit mechanics.
